posts.text:
ironing a t-shirt before leaving the house.

necessary ritual or just wasting time?

we just scrapped an entire production run because the shade of navy felt too aggressive in low light.

my team thinks i’m losing it.
most guys own ten jackets and wear the exact same one every single day regardless of the weather.

some people dress for their job.

others dress like they’re waiting for a flight to a city they’ve never been to.

which one are you.

buying a jacket three sizes too big because you saw it on a runway.

it never actually looks good, does it.

the guy at the coffee shop wearing a winter coat inside while it’s 70 degrees out.

commitment or insanity?

why is the hardware on expensive trousers always so unnecessarily heavy?

it feels like wearing a deadlift belt.

we spent weeks testing how the fabric bunches when you sit down.

if the garment doesn't move with you, i failed.

the guy who insists on buttoning every single button on his overshirt vs the guy who leaves it wide open.

there is a wrong answer.

why does every pair of trousers feel like they need a belt to stay at the right height?

if you have to cinch it that hard, the tailoring is lying to you.

the guy who spends an hour deciding on an outfit, only to realize he’s going to be the most overdressed person in the room.

we’ve all been there.

we removed the internal care tags on the latest batch. 

they were itchy, unnecessary, and felt like an afterthought.
the 2:00 PM coffee run is the only time you actually see what people wear when they aren't trying to impress the office.

black sneakers or white sneakers.

you can only keep one pair for the rest of your life.
there is a specific kind of confidence that comes from knowing your outfit isn't the most interesting thing in the room.
nothing ruins a good day like realizing your socks are sliding down into your shoes every ten minutes.
the best jacket you own is the one you don't even realize you have on until it starts raining.
we decided to skip the ribbed collar on the new batch. it stretches out too fast, even when it’s done right.

white crew socks: pulled up to the mid-calf or bunched down at the ankle. 

there is a definitive right way to do this.
the best-dressed person in the room is usually the one who hasn't looked at a trend report in years.

buying a garment because it looks good in a photo vs. how it actually moves during a commute.

most people only dress for the camera.

we chose a slightly denser cotton for the new restock. 

it makes the piece feel like it’s actually made of something. 

people either love the weight or they hate it.

that one hoodie you’ve had for six years that’s finally starting to thin out at the elbows.

throw it away or keep it forever?

the guys who iron their t-shirts versus the guys who let them air dry with the wrinkles.

which one are you.
everyone claims they value longevity, but most people can't stand the sight of a piece of clothing that shows actual signs of being worn.

i spent three hours staring at a pile of fabric scraps today just to figure out why the drape felt off by a millimeter.

most people think this stuff just happens.
nothing worse than buying a high-end item that forces you to constantly check if it's still sitting right on your body.
the specific relief of finding that one item in your closet that works with absolutely everything else you own.

the guy who washes his jeans every time he spills something versus the guy who never touches them with water. 

let’s settle this.

why is it so hard to find a simple sweater that doesn't lose its shape after three wears? 

stop making clothes for mannequins.
most people dress for the person they want to be, not the person they actually are on a Tuesday morning.

we spent three weeks arguing about the exact shade of grey for our next release. 

if it’s not neutral, it’s just noise.

the feeling of putting on a jacket you haven't worn in months and finding a twenty in the pocket. 

undefeated.

the guy who keeps his white sneakers clean vs the guy who believes they look better with a bit of wear.

be honest.

the guy who packs for a weekend trip in a single backpack versus the one who brings a full suitcase.

there is no middle ground.
there is nothing more exhausting than feeling like you have to rotate your wardrobe every three months to stay relevant.

most brands are obsessed with how their clothes look on a model in a studio.

i’m only interested in how they look after six hours of sitting at a desk.

we removed the internal tags from the new run.

nothing should be scratching your neck while you’re trying to think.

why is the lighting in every changing room designed to make you look like you’ve never seen the sun?

it’s impossible to judge a fit in there.

the guy who gets a haircut and immediately hates it for a week vs the guy who walks out ready for anything.

there is no in-between.

most people buy shoes for the aesthetic.

if you can’t walk five miles in them comfortably, they’re just expensive paperweights for your closet.

we experimented with a raw hem on a prototype today.

it looks unfinished. i think that might be exactly why i like it.

that feeling when you find a piece you love, buy it in every available color, and never shop for that item again.

that's peak efficiency.

hanging clothes on a wire hanger versus folding them properly in a drawer. 

you’re either one or the other.
why does every ‘essential’ list include a white button-down shirt that nobody actually wears past the office door?

the best style advice is just wearing the same thing until you stop thinking about how you look. 

confidence is forgetting you’re wearing clothes at all.
everyone claims they want a timeless wardrobe, but half the fun of getting dressed is being wrong about a fit once in a while.

we pushed back a launch because the zipper pull felt two grams too light. 

if you can feel the cost-cutting, it’s not worth wearing.

ironing a t-shirt before leaving the house: yes or no? 

i feel like there’s a line here.

why do we pretend that cuffing your pants is a design feature? 

most of us just couldn't find a tailor.

the most expensive piece in your closet is usually the one you wear the least. 

stop buying for the version of you that doesn't exist.

we skipped the chest pocket on the new long-sleeve. 

it just felt like extra weight that didn't need to be there.

late night at the airport, terminal 4, waiting for a delayed flight. 

the hoodies people are wearing tell a whole story.

black socks or white socks with shorts. 

you have to pick one forever.

why do we pretend that buying more clothes makes you feel like you have more options? 

it usually just creates more noise.

that guy who refuses to take his jacket off indoors. 

is he hiding a bad shirt or is he just cold?

we wasted two weeks sourcing a heavier thread for the cuffs. 

nobody will notice, but i definitely will.
the most honest version of your style is what you choose to wear on a lazy Sunday morning.

hoodies: do you pull the drawstring tight or leave them dangling loose?

it says more about how you move than you think.

the most overrated item in menswear is the tailored blazer.

most guys look like they’re wearing a costume, not an outfit.

the guy who buys sneakers solely for the gym vs the guy who wears them until the soles dissolve.

which one are you.

spending half an hour staring at a closet full of clothes and choosing the same grey tee you wore on tuesday.

we aren't as creative as we pretend to be.

we removed the neck label on the new collection. it took longer to source a heat-press machine than to design the shirt.

itchy necks are a design failure.

buying boots just to keep them clean is a strange way to spend money.

if you aren't scuffing them, you aren't using them.
the worst part of any morning is realizing the shirt you wanted to wear is still damp from the wash.
do you tuck in your t-shirt, or is that just a fast track to feeling uncomfortable all day?

you can tell how someone actually spends their time by the wear pattern on their denim.

there is no faking that.

i spent two hours debating whether the side seams should sit forward or back.

my friends think i’m insane, but the fit is perfect now.

the guy who wears sunglasses inside a dimly lit coffee shop.

confident or just hiding?

a belt either pulls an outfit together or ruins the line completely.

there is no middle ground.

the most exhausting part of menswear is the obsession with 'versatility.'

sometimes a piece should just do one thing perfectly.

people say you should dress for the job you want.

i’ve always found that the best way to get nothing done.

we finally settled on the hem weight for the new knitwear.

it feels like a paperweight, exactly how i wanted it.

when the cuff of your pants hits the floor and frays.

do you trim it or leave it to show you actually walk places?

why does every dressing room have lighting that makes everyone look like a hospital patient?

it’s hard to judge a fit when you look ill.

most people buy clothes for the version of themselves they want to be on saturday night.

forget that. dress for your 2pm meeting on a tuesday.

that one guy who wears the exact same silhouette every day of the year.

he’s not uninspired. he’s just figured it out.

we skipped the chest pocket on the new button-downs.

it ruins the drape and nobody actually keeps anything in there anyway.

wearing a coat over a hoodie. 

layering genius or just trying too hard to look busy?

most guys buy gear for a mountain expedition they’ll never actually book. 

stop dressing for the hobby you wish you had.

the quiet guy in the room wearing a perfect heavy-weight tee. 

he’s usually the one who actually knows what he’s doing.

that feeling when you find a piece you love and immediately want to buy it in every color. 

is that smart shopping or a lack of imagination?

tried to simplify our production process this month. 

ended up adding three extra steps just to make the hem sit perfectly flat. i don't think i'll ever learn.

zippers vs. buttons on a jacket. 

you can only choose one for the rest of your life.

the most honest way to tell if a guy has good taste? 

look at his socks. it always gives the game away.

trying to find a decent hat that doesn't have a massive billboard on the front is a full-time job. 

why is this so hard?
the best piece of clothing you own is the one you haven't washed in three weeks because you’re terrified of ruining the fit.

i refused to use a specific type of sewing machine for our latest run because the stitch tension was off by a fraction of a millimeter. 

my production lead thinks i’m losing it.

sneakers or boots. 

you can only keep one style for the rest of your life.

most people think a capsule wardrobe is about having fewer clothes. 

it’s actually about having zero room for stuff you don’t reach for every single week.
everyone talks about the fit of the shoulders, but the weight of the collar is what actually changes the entire look.
that moment when you realize you’ve been wearing the same two pairs of pants for a month because nothing else in the closet feels right.

i spent all morning trying to convince myself that a slightly tapered fit was a good idea. 

ended up cutting it straight. much cleaner.

black or navy for the base layer.

you can only pick one for the rest of your life.

the guy wearing a hoodie under a suit jacket.

genius move or just looking for attention?

why does every laundry detergent smell like a synthetic forest or a chemical ocean?

i just want my clothes to smell like nothing.

the most expensive piece in your closet is usually the one you wear the least.

we all have that one mistake hanging there.

we pulled the final sample off the line today and the weight was still slightly off for my liking.

back to the drawing board for another two weeks.

the guy who wears a plain grey sweatshirt to a wedding. 

respect or total lack of effort?

most guys iron their shirts. 

i let the weight of the fabric do the work.
